from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: Why Do We Model Outbreaks?", [
            "Epidemics spread through susceptible populations rapidly.",
            "One spark ignites a wildfire of infection.",
            "We must predict the outbreak's peak impact."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show population nodes with '#FFFFFF' label 'Healthy'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(9)])
        positions = ['B2', 'B3', 'B4', 'C2', 'C3', 'C4', 'D2', 'D3', 'D4']
        for i, pos in enumerate(positions):
            self.place_at_grid(nodes[i], pos, scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(nodes))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Introduce an 'Outbreak' indicator icon with '#FF0000'.
        # Visualize connection lines spreading between nodes.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        spark = Star(color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(spark, 'C3')
        
        connections = VGroup(*[
            Line(nodes[i].get_center(), nodes[j].get_center(), color="#AAAAAA", stroke_width=2)
            for i, j in [(1, 0), (1, 2), (1, 4), (4, 3), (4, 5), (4, 7), (7, 6), (7, 8)]
        ])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(spark), Create(connections))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        peak_label = Text("Peak Impact", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(peak_label, 'E5')
        self.play(Write(peak_label))
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Epidemics involve movement between distinct population states.", "Rates determine how fast transitions occur daily.", "Think of flow filling an epidemic bucket."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Population Dynamics & Rates", lecture_lines)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "SIR defines three key population states.",
            "Susceptible people haven't been infected yet.",
            "Infected individuals are currently spreading the virus.",
            "Recovered individuals are now immune to reinfection.",
            "These states track the entire disease progression."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The SIR Framework: Defining the States", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        s_box = Square(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.6, color="#0000FF").set_fill("#0000FF", opacity=0.6)
        i_box = Square(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.6, color="#FF0000").set_fill("#FF0000", opacity=0.6)
        r_box = Square(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.6, color="#00FF00").set_fill("#00FF00", opacity=0.6)
        
        s_text = Text("S", font_size=36, color="#FFFFFF")
        i_text = Text("I", font_size=36, color="#FFFFFF")
        r_text = Text("R", font_size=36, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        s_group = VGroup(s_box, s_text)
        i_group = VGroup(i_box, i_text)
        r_group = VGroup(r_box, r_text)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(s_group, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(s_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(i_group, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(i_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(r_group, 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(r_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        arrow1 = Arrow(s_group.get_right(), i_group.get_left(), color="#FFFFFF")
        arrow2 = Arrow(i_group.get_right(), r_group.get_left(), color="#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Transmission happens through interactions between populations.",
            "Infections occur as susceptible meet infected individuals.",
            "Recovery flows from infected to removed states.",
            "We model these using differential transition equations.",
            "Equations show how infection and recovery change."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Mechanics: The Transition Equations", lecture_lines)
        
        # Prepare equations
        eq_ds = MathTex(r"\frac{dS}{dt} = -\beta \frac{SI}{N}", font_size=36)
        eq_di = MathTex(r"\frac{dI}{dt} = \beta \frac{SI}{N} - \gamma I", font_size=36)
        eq_dr = MathTex(r"\frac{dR}{dt} = \gamma I", font_size=36)
        
        eqs = VGroup(eq_ds, eq_di, eq_dr).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(eqs, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(eq_ds))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#ADD8E6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(eq_di))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#ADD8E6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(eq_dr))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ADD8E6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Already shown in the structural buildup
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight terms as requested
        term_inf = MathTex(r"\beta \frac{SI}{N}", color="#FF0000").move_to(eq_di[0][5:11])
        term_rec = MathTex(r"\gamma I", color="#00FF00").move_to(eq_dr[0][4:6])
        
        self.play(eq_di[0][5:11].animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
                  eq_dr[0][4:6].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Adjusting transmission variables can flatten curves.",
            "Social distancing reduces the infection peak significantly.",
            "Predictive models guide effective public health policy."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Simulation & Application: 'Flattening the Curve'", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create graphs representing infection curves
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[0, 10, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.6)
        curve_high = axes.plot(lambda x: 8 * np.exp(-(x - 4)**2 / 2), color=RED)
        curve_low = axes.plot(lambda x: 4 * np.exp(-(x - 5)**2 / 4), color=GREEN)
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve_high))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Transform(curve_high, curve_low))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        target_icon = Dot(color=GREEN).scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(target_icon, "D6")
        self.play(FadeIn(target_icon))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Decoding Epidemics: The Mechanics of the SIR Model
outline.target_audience: University students (Introductory STEM or Public Health)

sections.title: Introduction: Why Do We Model Outbreaks?
sections.content: A brief overview of how epidemics spread in populations. Define the core objective: Predicting the 'peak' of infections and the impact of intervention.
sections.example: A campfire analogy: One spark (infected) hits a dry forest (susceptible), quickly turning into a wildfire (epidemic) before running out of fuel (recovered/immune).

sections.title: Prerequisite: Population Dynamics & Rates
sections.content: Establish the concept of flow. Introduce the idea that individuals transition between states at specific rates (represented as arrows in a flow diagram).
sections.example: A faucet filling a bucket: The rate of flow determines how fast the level changes. Here, 'flow' = number of people changing status per day.

sections.title: The SIR Framework: Defining the States
sections.content: Visual breakdown of the three compartments: S (Susceptible), I (Infected), and R (Recovered/Removed). Use a color-coded diagram (Green -> Red -> Blue).
sections.example: A game of Tag: Children who haven't been tagged (S), those currently 'It' (I), and those sitting out on the bench because they've already played (R).

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics: The Transition Equations
sections.content: Explain the logic of transmission (S+I interaction) and recovery (I -> R). Visualize this using a graph: 'Infection Rate' curve vs. 'Recovery Rate' curve.
sections.example: An animated bar chart showing the S-bar shrinking, the I-bar spiking, and the R-bar steadily growing over a 30-day timeline.

sections.title: Simulation & Application: 'Flattening the Curve'
sections.content: Show how changing transmission variables (e.g., social distancing) flattens the peak of the 'I' curve. Summarize the model's predictive power for public health policy.
sections.example: Simulating a scenario where a digital population of robots reduces their contact rate, showing the Red 'Infection' peak drop significantly on the graph.
